name: GAO and DoD Inspector General findings on C2, interoperability, networks, data and software
summary: Across 2019-2026, GAO and the DoD Inspector General document a consistent pattern in the C4ISR ecosystem: the joint C2 concept (JADC2/CJADC2) was launched in 2019 without defined contributing systems, a resourced/authoritative coordinating body, or (as of April 2025) any framework to guide investments or measure progress, so the services continue to build C2 'largely in isolation' while 'overly restrictive data classification' blocks data sharing and no DOD entity owns that problem (GAO-23-105495, GAO-25-106454). Domain programs show the same shape: ABMS began without a plan or cost estimate (GAO-20-389); Space C2 replacement has been late and over budget 'for decades' with SPADOC still in use in 2023 (GAO-20-146, GAO-22-104685, GAO-23-105920); GPS M-code and alternative PNT lag with proprietary receivers that 'cannot be upgraded affordably' (GAO-21-320SP, GAO-24-106841); EMSO governance was found deficient (GAO-21-64). Cross-cutting enablers are repeatedly flagged: weapon programs still use waterfall despite the 2020 software pathway (GAO-23-105867); IT programs miss zero-trust and metrics requirements (GAO-24-106912, GAO-25-107649); MOSA is legally required but rarely planned or enforced and vendor licensing practices restrict cloud portability (GAO-25-106931, GAO-23-106290); AI acquisition lacks usable data, skilled staff, guidance and lessons-learned capture (GAO-22-104765 through GAO April 2026); and enterprise data/AI governance is unstable (DODIG-2025-039 on CDAO, DoD IG 2026 Advana audit with 10 of 12 recommendations rejected, Advana's recompete cancellation and split into the War Data Platform). GAO's 2026 annual assessment says average capability delivery now exceeds 12 years while acquisition staffing shrank in 2025. DoD leadership itself now names ATOs, data sharing and classification as 'blockers' to be eliminated (Jan 2026 AI strategy memo), and DoD CIO's 2025 DevSecOps study records authorizing officials 'biased to caution' and unclear reciprocity. Evidence is thin or unretrievable for DCGS, Project Overmatch, NGC2, JWCC performance, contested-logistics C2 and the substantive findings of DODIG-2025-126 on mission-partner sharing; absence of reports there is not evidence of absence of problems. For founders, the oversight record validates persistent demand for interoperability/translation, classification-aware data handling, ATO/compliance acceleration, open-architecture PNT/fusion software and data-quality tooling, but also shows that buyers are fragmented, under-staffed, and prone to program restructuring, so revenue evidence must come from repeat orders rather than from prototype awards or contract ceilings.

findings.title: GAO-25-106454: six years into CJADC2, DOD still has no framework to guide investments or track progress; services build C2 in isolation
findings.detail: GAO's April 8, 2025 report (requested by a House report) found DOD 'has attempted to define and guide CJADC2 efforts since its inception' in 2019 but 'has yet to build a framework that can guide CJADC2-related investments across DOD or track progress toward its goals.' Military departments and other DOD entities 'have concurrently pursued their own independent data integration capabilities.' GAO interviewed all 11 combatant commands and the CJADC2 cross-functional team. CJADC2 is described as 'not itself a system' but a way to use data and analytics; the target is moving from a 'swivel chair' model (analyst manually re-keys data between systems) to an integrated model.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: In the absence of clear direction, warfighting entities will continue to pursue their command and control projects largely in isolation, which will likely result in achieving CJADC2 much more slowly and inefficiently, if at all.
findings.source_title: Defense Command and Control: Further Progress Hinges on Establishing a Comprehensive Framework (GAO-25-106454)

findings.title: GAO-25-106454: overly restrictive data classification is a 'significant hindrance' to sharing C2 data, and no DOD entity owns the fix
findings.detail: GAO found 'several critical challenges to achieving CJADC2 that DOD has yet to formally identify and address.' The example given is 'overly restrictive data classification' as 'a significant hindrance to sharing command and control data.' Officials 'were not aware of an entity working on a solution to this or several other critical challenges,' and CJADC2 leadership told GAO 'addressing these challenges was beyond their purview.' GAO recommended the Secretary of Defense 'identify, comprehensively assess, and address key challenges.' MeriTalk (Apr 8, 2025) confirms the quotes and that DOD 'mostly concurred.'
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Overly restrictive data classification is a significant hindrance to sharing command and control data. Further, officials GAO spoke with were not aware of an entity working on a solution to this or several other critical challenges.
findings.source_title: GAO-25-106454 (Highlights) and MeriTalk coverage 'GAO Pushes DoD to Create Framework for CJADC2 Investments'
pain_keywords: not aware of an entity working on a solution
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Points to demand for classification-aware data handling, automated tagging/downgrade workflows and cross-domain solutions; however, CDS is an NSA/NCDSMO-accredited, ITAR/clearance-heavy niche that is hard for a two-student, non-U.S.-person-founder team to enter directly.

findings.title: GAO-25-106454: no mechanism to share lessons learned from CJADC2 experimentation, risking duplicative efforts
findings.detail: GAO found DOD 'is conducting activities aimed at demonstrating selected capabilities, but there is limited awareness of experimentation lessons learned that could lead to duplicative efforts and slower progress toward CJADC2 goals.' Three recommendations: (1) a framework to evaluate whether military organization investments align with CJADC2 goals, with clear guidance for C2 investments and a means to track progress; (2) an approach to consolidate and share lessons learned from experimentation and real-world activities; (3) identify and address key challenges. DOD concurred with two and partially concurred with one.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DOD is conducting activities aimed at demonstrating selected capabilities, but there is limited awareness of experimentation lessons learned that could lead to duplicative efforts and slower progress toward CJADC2 goals.

findings.title: GAO-23-105495: JADC2 details undefined; the JADC2 Cross-Functional Team lacked personnel and authority to direct other offices
findings.detail: GAO's January 13, 2023 report found DOD 'has not yet defined the details, such as which existing systems will contribute to JADC2 and what future capabilities need to be developed.' Bloomberg (Jan 13 and Jan 17, 2023) reported that the Pentagon told GAO the cross-functional team it established to coordinate JADC2 and set priorities 'lacks the personnel to complete its task,' that GAO 'determined the team lacks authority to direct other offices,' and that an Air Force review recommended 10 additional personnel to be included in the Joint Staff's FY2024 budget request. DOD had a Dec. 31, 2022 deadline for a tools/cost/schedule response.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The Pentagon told GAO that a cross-functional team it established to coordinate the effort and set priorities lacks the personnel to complete its task, and GAO determined the team lacks authority to direct other offices.

findings.title: GAO-20-389: Air Force had no complete plan, cost estimate or affordability analysis for ABMS; management structure and decision authority not formalized
findings.detail: GAO's April 16, 2020 report found the Air Force 'hasn't developed a complete plan for the system - like identifying which technologies would be' matured. GAO recommended the Air Force develop and brief Congress quarterly on a plan to mature technologies, a cost estimate and an affordability analysis, and formalize the ABMS management structure and decision-making authorities. ABMS was described as a cloud-based data-sharing network connecting sensors on drones, aircraft, ships and other weapon systems to produce a real-time operational picture across domains.

findings.title: GAO-20-146: three prior space C2 programs ran late and over budget; legacy SPADOC operates on a mainframe discontinued in 1998; Space C2 adopted Agile before DOD guidance existed

SPADOC 'is now significantly beyond its estimated end-of-life, and is operating on an outdated computer mainframe - production of which was discontinued in 1998.' A 2026 systems-engineering knowledge pack summarizing GAO's Agile work describes Space C2 as 'one of the first DOD software-intensive programs to move from Waterfall into an Agile framework while the governing acquisition guidance did not yet cover Agile' (guidance lag).

findings.title: GAO-25-107649 (June 2025): of 24 major DOD IT business programs ($10.9B FY23-25), 2 had no cybersecurity strategy, 4 had no zero-trust plan for the 2027 deadline, and only 11 used Agile
findings.detail: GAO's June 12, 2025 IT Systems Annual Assessment reviewed 24 programs. Two 'didn't have a strategy in place to reduce cybersecurity threats'; four 'hadn't developed plans to implement ... zero trust architecture by the 2027 deadline'; 22 of 24 reported an approved cybersecurity strategy and 20 of 24 reported implementing zero trust. Eleven of 24 used Agile, but 3 of those 11 did not use required metrics/tools for customer satisfaction and progress. Fourteen programs reported cost and/or schedule changes since Jan 2023 (cost increases $6.1M-$815.5M, median $173.5M; delays 3-48 months, median 15 months). Persistence: GAO's June 2022 assessment found 10 programs without an approved cybersecurity strategy; by March 2025 two still lacked one. The Washington Post (Sep 17, 2026) cited this report while describing 'cybersecurity modernization debt that the Pentagon has never fully paid.'
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Four programs had not developed plans to implement zero trust architecture in their cybersecurity frameworks by DOD's 2027 deadline. GAO will continue to monitor the department's progress.
findings.source_title: IT Systems Annual Assessment: DOD Needs to Improve Performance Reporting and Cybersecurity Planning (GAO-25-107649); MeriTalk, TechRadar, The Register coverage

findings.title: GAO-25-106931 (Jan 2025): only 14 of 20 programs implemented MOSA to some extent; none analyzed MOSA costs vs. benefits; 14 recommendations; GAO official says MOSA implementation still lagging (June 2026)
findings.detail: GAO reviewed 20 programs started after 2016 MOSA legislation. 'GAO found that 14 of the 20 programs it reviewed reported implementing a MOSA to at least some extent. Other programs cited barriers ... such as added cost and time.' 'None of the 20 programs GAO reviewed conducted a formal analysis of costs and benefits for a MOSA because DOD's policy does not explicitly require one.' 'Most programs did not address all key MOSA planning elements.' GAO made 14 recommendations; DOD concurred. Defense Daily (Jun 10, 2026) reported a GAO official saying that although MOSA has been required for MDAPs since Jan 2019 and other acquisitions since Jan 2021, 'few programs are implementing the standard.' An HII executive (Nov 2025) argued acquisition 'continues to prioritize closed, proprietary architectures' and warned venture-backed startups could 'replace one proprietary problem with another.'
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: None of the 20 programs GAO reviewed conducted a formal analysis of costs and benefits for a MOSA because DOD's policy does not explicitly require one ... DOD's process for coordinating MOSAs across portfolios does not ensure the level of collaboration needed.
findings.source_title: Weapon Systems Acquisition: DOD Needs Better Planning to Attain Benefits of Modular Open Systems (GAO-25-106931); Defense Daily 'MOSA Implementation By Pentagon Lagging, GAO Official Says'

findings.startup_relevance: Open-interface compliance is both a policy tailwind and a trap: programs say they want MOSA but rarely enforce it, and incumbents 'resist sharing interface specifications,' which is exactly the moat a small integrator must penetrate.

findings.title: GAO-21-320SP (May 2021): alternative PNT is not prioritized, has no central program office, unclear requirements, and closed proprietary PNT systems leave 'few opportunities to integrate' new sources
findings.detail: GAO's technology assessment (full text retrieved via a GitHub mirror of the PDF) found: 'Officials from across DOD and experts told GAO that alternative PNT solutions are not prioritized within DOD. For example, there is no central program office responsible for developing the variety of alternative PNT technologies.' 'DOD's continued reliance on GPS, despite known GPS vulnerabilities ... presents a challenge for obtaining sufficient support to develop viable alternatives.' 'Challenges in establishing clear PNT performance requirements hinder technology development.' An official said that 'because of this proprietary nature, there are few opportunities to integrate alternative PNT technologies'; DOD's PNT open-architecture (MOSA) initiative and the Army's PNT Operating System fusion engine aim to standardize interfaces. GAO offered six policy options (collaboration, resiliency focus, clarify requirements, coordinate with industry, etc.).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: There is no central program office responsible for developing the variety of alternative PNT technologies across DOD ... The official stated that, because of this proprietary nature, there are few opportunities to integrate alternative PNT technologies.
findings.source_title: Defense Navigation Capabilities: DOD is Developing Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Technologies to Complement GPS (GAO-21-320SP)

findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Software-defined PNT fusion engines conforming to DOD's open architecture are an entry point for a small team, but the market is hardware-adjacent, export-controlled and dominated by Collins/L3Harris/BAE receiver incumbents.

findings.title: GAO August 2022 PNT report (public version of an April 2022 report): 'even with these upgrades, vulnerabilities will remain'; current receivers 'cannot be upgraded affordably'
findings.detail: European Security (May 5, 2025) summarized a GAO report published August 2022 (public version of a report issued April 2022 that omitted 'sensitive details about seven of the 11 alternative PNT technology and product development efforts'). GAO warned that despite M-code and anti-jam antennas 'even with these upgrades, vulnerabilities will remain,' and that 'current PNT receivers are not designed to easily add in new sources of PNT information... these systems cannot be upgraded affordably.' GAO report number not captured in this sweep.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Current PNT receivers are not designed to easily add in new sources of PNT information... these systems cannot be upgraded affordably.
findings.source_title: European Security, 'GPS under threat' (citing GAO August 2022 report)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Reinforces the open-architecture PNT receiver/fusion opportunity and the retrofit problem for the installed base.

findings.title: GAO-24-106841 (Sept 2024): GPS M-code delays continue across ground, space and user-equipment segments
findings.detail: GAO found DOD 'has been working for years to upgrade GPS with a military-specific signal known as M-code that resists interference or jamming. Amid ongoing delays, DOD has made some progress ... But DOD faces challenges with all 3 segments.' Ground segment modernization finished some key testing but more testing and demonstration are needed. Topic tags include 'Radio receiver' and 'Software'.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Amid ongoing delays, DOD has made some progress developing the necessary ground, space, and user equipment to use M-code. But DOD faces challenges with all 3 segments.
findings.source_title: GPS Modernization: Delays Continue in Delivering More Secure Capability for the Warfighter (GAO-24-106841)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Persistence evidence for PNT resilience demand through 2024; a startup cannot fix M-code but can sell around it (alt-PNT, jamming detection, PNT assurance software).

findings.title: GAO-21-64 / GAO-21-440T: DOD electromagnetic spectrum operations suffer governance and oversight gaps; 'U.S. risks losing control of the battlefield'; Russia's EW forces 'world class'
findings.detail: GAO's December 10, 2020 report and March 19, 2021 testimony: 'The U.S. risks losing control of the battlefield if it doesn't control the electromagnetic spectrum, according to the Defense Department ... Russian electromagnetic warfare forces, described by the Defense Intelligence Agency as world class, have demonstrated effectiveness in real-world applications against U.S. and foreign militaries. China also has advanced capabilities. Earlier strategies' had not been fully implemented. GAO recommended DOD address governance and oversight issues; Forbes (Dec 2022) noted the Pentagon largely concurred. A narrower GAO report (June 5, 2026) on DOD-NTIA spectrum coordination found DOD 'generally follows leading collaboration practices' for frequency assignments, so the later report does not show the 2020 governance findings resolved or persisting.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The U.S. risks losing control of the battlefield if it doesn't control the electromagnetic spectrum, according to the Defense Department.
findings.source_title: Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations: DOD Needs to Address Governance and Oversight Issues to Help Ensure Superiority (GAO-21-64); testimony GAO-21-440T
chain_steps: GAO Jun 2026 spectrum coordination report (narrower scope)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: EMSO planning/management software (EMBM) is an underdeveloped C2 sub-market with documented leadership gaps; however, much of the relevant data is classified and the customer set (Joint EMSO Center, service EW cells) is small.

findings.title: GAO AI series (2022-2023): DOD AI acquisition hampered by long acquisition processes, staff shortages and insufficient usable training data; strategies and inventory incomplete; no department-wide AI acquisition guidance
findings.detail: GAO-22-104765 (Feb 17, 2022): 'DOD's efforts to acquire AI come with some challenges that DOD usually faces, such as DOD's long acquisition processes and shortages of skilled staff, as well as AI-specific challenges like having enough usable data to train the AI.' GAO-22-105834 (Mar 30, 2022): 'DOD's AI-related strategies could be more comprehensive ... In addition, DOD has not yet issued' [collaboration guidance]; recommended improving strategies, inventory process and collaboration guidance. GAO-23-105850 (Jun 29, 2023): 'DOD Needs Department-Wide Guidance to Inform Acquisitions'; 13 private companies stressed intellectual property and data rights in AI contracts. Note: one third-party GitHub whitepaper mis-cites GAO-22-105834 as a JADC2 report; the GAO metadata mirror confirms it is the AI strategies/inventory report.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DOD's efforts to acquire AI come with some challenges that DOD usually faces, such as DOD's long acquisition processes and shortages of skilled staff, as well as AI-specific challenges like having enough usable data to train the AI.
findings.source_title: Artificial Intelligence: Status of Developing and Acquiring Capabilities for Weapon Systems (GAO-22-104765); GAO-22-105834; GAO-23-105850
chain_steps: GAO Feb/Mar 2022 strategy and inventory gaps
pain_keywords: usable data to train the AI
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: The 'not enough usable data' finding is the root cause that data-labeling, data-fabric and synthetic-data startups sell against; IP/data-rights clauses are the contracting battleground.

findings.title: GAO-24-105645 (Dec 2023): DOD cannot fully identify its AI workforce or which positions need AI skills
findings.detail: GAO found DOD 'has invested billions of dollars to integrate artificial intelligence into its operations,' including analyzing ISR data, but 'DOD can't fully identify who is part of its AI workforce or which positions require personnel with AI skills. As a result, DOD can't effectively assess the state of its AI' workforce. Epoch Times (May 2025) also summarized a GAO finding that DOD had almost $2B budgeted for AI in 2024 but 'couldn't fully identify' how it planned to use the money (report not verified in this sweep).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DOD can't fully identify who is part of its AI workforce or which positions require personnel with AI skills.
findings.source_title: Artificial Intelligence: Actions Needed to Improve DOD's Workforce Management (GAO-24-105645)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Skills scarcity inside government favors vendors that deliver turnkey analytics rather than toolkits requiring in-house data scientists.

findings.title: GAO April 2026: DOD and three other agencies are not systematically collecting lessons learned from AI acquisitions (13 acquisitions, 44 contracts reviewed); all four recommendations concurred
findings.detail: GAO's April 2026 report 'Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions: Agencies Should Collect and Apply Lessons Learned to Improve Future Procurements' reviewed 13 AI acquisitions at DOD, DHS, GSA and VA and analyzed 44 AI contracts/agreements (Sept 2018-Feb 2025). Agencies 'were not yet systematically collecting lessons learned ... a necessary first step to share knowledge'; officials said 'their agency policies did not require them to collect lessons learned,' so agencies miss best practices 'such as contract terms related to data rights or testing requirements.' Officials reported difficulty accessing AI technical experts to evaluate proposals and understanding AI-related costs. Federal AI use reportedly more than doubled 2023-2024. GAO report number not captured.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The agencies are missing opportunities to identify and apply best practices - such as contract terms related to data rights or testing requirements - or to avoid mistakes as agencies increasingly acquire AI.
findings.source_title: GAO, Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions: Agencies Should Collect and Apply Lessons Learned to Improve Future Procurements (April 2026); FedScoop, HSToday, BiometricUpdate coverage
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Government-side evaluation capacity for AI is thin; startups that bring their own test-and-evaluation evidence and clear data-rights terms reduce friction for buyers.

findings.title: DODIG-2025-039 (Nov 14, 2024): CDAO operated without a charter or implementation plan; CDAO and DoD CIO disputed boundaries over cloud/IT infrastructure
findings.detail: Per an independent blog (revised July 17, 2026) that cites the redacted report and DoDD 5105.89: the DoD OIG found CDAO 'was still operating without several foundational documents needed to make its responsibilities clear'; as of June 2024 the implementation plan for the 2023 Data, Analytics and AI Adoption Strategy and the chartering directive/instruction 'remained in draft.' 'CDAO and the DoD CIO disagreed about parts of the boundary around digital infrastructure, information technology, cloud systems, and related responsibilities.' OIG made two recommendations (implementation plan with performance measures; complete directive/instruction); one closed, one resolved-open. DoD issued DoDD 5105.89 on Nov 18, 2024. CDAO was later realigned under USD(R&E) (Aug 2025). The dodig.mil report page could not be fetched directly.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: CDAO and the DoD Chief Information Officer disagreed about parts of the boundary around digital infrastructure, information technology, cloud systems, and related responsibilities. Both offices were concerned about overlap.
findings.source_title: DoD OIG, Evaluation of the Effectiveness of the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office's AI Governance and Acquisition Process (DODIG-2025-039), as summarized by Bruce B. A. West, 'The CDAO evaluation was really about decision rights'
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Explains why enterprise data/AI buying authority at OSD is unstable; startups should target service-level program offices or combatant-command pilots rather than CDAO-centric enterprise deals.

findings.title: DoD IG Advana audit (May 2026): CDAO did not implement NIST interface controls; 78 of 387 source systems connected without data-sharing agreements; 10 of 12 recommendations rejected
findings.detail: MeriTalk (May 18, 2026) reported a DoD IG audit finding that OCDAO 'did not implement effective interface controls between Advana and non-financial source systems' per NIST SP 800-53, leaving 'limited assurance' that data transferred are accurate and complete, with the warning that 'inaccurate or incomplete data could lead DOD leaders to make misinformed decisions affecting operations.' Specifics: no data sharing agreements with 78 of 387 source systems before connection; privileged access for 26 of 29 privileged users not based on accurate/complete request forms; no effective user-access monitoring, validation checks, or error notification to system owners. Officials cited beliefs that NIST did not apply to all source systems, high staff turnover and personnel shortages. Twelve recommendations; the deputy under secretary for R&E (for OCDAO) agreed with two and disagreed with ten, including immediate data-sharing agreements. Advana aggregates data from 437 systems. Report number not captured.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Without effective interface controls, OCDAO has limited assurance that data transferred between source systems and Advana are accurate and complete.
findings.source_title: MeriTalk, 'DOD IG Flags Advana Interface Control Weaknesses, Raising Data Accuracy Issues' (summarizing DoD OIG audit)
chain_steps: IG audit May 2026: interface controls, DSAs missing
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: The enterprise data platform's data-quality plumbing (ingest validation, lineage, agreements, access governance) is officially deficient; data-quality/observability tooling for government data lakes is a credible wedge, though the CDAO's non-concurrence shows resistance to added process.

findings.title: Advana instability 2024-2026: development paused (June 2024), $15B AAMAC recompete canceled (July 2025), 80% contractor cuts reported, split into the War Data Platform (Jan 2026), $821M Accenture integration award (July 2026)
findings.detail: Defense One (Aug 20, 2025): Advana, launched 2021 with a five-year $674M Booz Allen contract, reached ~20,000 users in 42 organizations within months and 72,000+ users by 2023; CDAO paused development in June 2024 to strengthen architecture; a defense official said 'you cut contracted staff by 80 percent and you have a turnover of close to ... 60 percent? Things are going to break.' The article notes DoD IG in July 2022 'chided elements of the military for not adopting it fast enough' and that Advana became the key data platform for operational logistics and Joint Staff planning, including 'contested logistics' wargames. Washington Technology/MeriTalk (Jul 24, 2025): the $15B Advancing AI Multiple Award Contract draft solicitation was canceled, 'program is currently on hold.' MeriTalk (Jan 16, 2026): Secretary Hegseth directed splitting Advana, whose growth produced a 'complex technical architecture' requiring 'rationalization,' into a War Data Platform. MeriTalk (Jul 10, 2026): Accenture received $821M for War Data Platform integration. AEI (Sep 11, 2026) notes the WDP 'endures acquisition strategy confusion.'
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: You tell this organization to do 'A.' Then you cut contracted staff by 80 percent and you have a turnover of close to what, 60 percent? Things are going to break. Things are going to get delayed.
findings.source_title: Defense One, 'Pentagon reductions set back critical AI-data platform'; Washington Technology; MeriTalk; AEI 'Advancing the War Data Platform'
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Enterprise data-platform contracting is in flux and being consolidated with large integrators; small vendors are more likely to enter as plug-ins/data products than as platform owners. Contract values cited are awards/ceilings, not revenue.

findings.title: GAO weapon systems annual assessments 2021-2026: delivery keeps slowing (average >12 years), new pathways not clearly faster, workforce losses (40 of 48 programs) after 2025 deferred-resignation program
findings.detail: GAO-21-222 (Jun 2021) 'Updated Program Oversight Approach Needed'; GAO-22-105230 (Jun 2022) 'Challenges to Fielding Capabilities Faster Persist'; GAO-23-106059 (Jun 2023): delays driven by 'supplier, software, and design problems,' recommended updating MOSA policy; GAO-24-106831 (Jun 17, 2024) 'DOD Is Not Yet Well-Positioned to Field Systems with Speed' - 'some programs in the new pathways likely won't deliver much faster than traditional programs' (DoD CIO's March 2025 DevSecOps study cites this report as finding 75-80% of 40 MDAPs adopted modern practices and almost half deliver software in under four months); GAO-25-107569 (2025) 'DOD Leaders Should Ensure That Newer Programs Are Structured for Speed and Innovation'; July 2, 2026 assessment (per MeriTalk/NewsMax/PubT): average time to deliver a capability has grown to more than 12 years; 40 of 48 programs reported workforce issues; 37 reported staffing reductions; 48,000+ DOD employees (6.3%) approved for the deferred resignation program Jan-Jun 2025; DOD plans at least $49B across 23 middle-tier programs; MTA policy does not require mature technologies at start (DOD concurred).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Despite years of acquisition reform, the DoW still struggles to field new capabilities rapidly ... the average time required to deliver a capability has grown to more than 12 years.
findings.source_title: GAO Weapon Systems Annual Assessments (GAO-21-222, GAO-22-105230, GAO-23-106059, GAO-24-106831, GAO-25-107569, and the July 2, 2026 assessment as reported by MeriTalk)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Program-office capacity is shrinking while mandates to go faster grow; this creates demand for vendor-provided integration and test capacity, but also lengthens government decision cycles that a bootstrapped startup must survive.

findings.title: GAO-23-105008 (Feb 2023): middle-tier rapid prototyping/fielding requires changes to oversight and development approaches
findings.detail: GAO's February 7, 2023 report on Middle-Tier Defense Acquisitions found rapid prototyping and fielding 'requires changes to oversight and development approaches.' The 2026 annual assessment reiterates that DOD policy 'does not clearly require programs entering the middle tier acquisition pathway to begin with mature technologies.'
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Rapid prototyping and fielding requires changes to oversight and development approaches.
findings.source_title: Middle-Tier Defense Acquisitions: Rapid Prototyping and Fielding Requires Changes to Oversight and Development Approaches (GAO-23-105008)
chain_steps: GAO Jul 2026 rec on technology maturity
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: MTA and OTA prototyping are the routes most NGC2/ABMS vendors used; GAO's persistent critique implies continued policy churn around these routes.

findings.title: GAO-24-107566 (July 2024): Army fielded 6 new equipment priorities ($46.5B) but sometimes fielded before support was in place
findings.detail: GAO found that since FY2021 the Army used new approaches to rapidly develop equipment, fielded six new priorities including upgraded air and missile defenses, and 'invested $46.5 billion in these efforts. But sometimes, the Army has put new equipment into the field' before maintenance/support, training and other enablers were ready; actions needed to support fielding. This is the only 2019-2026 GAO report on Army modernization fielding located; no GAO or DoD IG report specifically on the Integrated Tactical Network / Capability Sets was found in this sweep (public evidence insufficient).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: It has invested $46.5 billion in these efforts. But sometimes, the Army has put new equipment into the field [before support was ready].
findings.source_title: Army Modernization: Actions Needed to Support Fielding New Equipment (GAO-24-107566)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Fielding-support gaps (training, sustainment, help desk) around new network kit are a services/software opportunity adjacent to NGC2 scaling.

findings.title: Army tactical network: GAO documented 'nearly 20 years' of limited success (2013-2014); no 2019-2026 GAO/IG ITN report found; NGC2 now absorbs the effort with mixed field reports (Sept 2026)
findings.detail: GAO-13-179 (Jan 2013): 'For nearly 20 years, the Army has had limited success in developing an information network with sensors, software, and radios'; GAO-13-711 (Aug 2013): the network was the Army's number one modernization priority at roughly $3 billion per year indefinitely; GAO-14-460 (May 2014) on competition. The GAO metadata mirror shows no 2019-2026 GAO report on ITN or Capability Sets, and DoD IG audits on ITN were not locatable (Public evidence insufficient). Persistence signals from non-GAO sources: Army FY2027 request includes $904M NGC2 R&D (Defense News, May 2026); Anduril-led NGC2 prototype OTA $99.6M (Jul 2025); Persistent Systems MANET orders $34M (Oct 2025) + $87.5M (Feb 2026); L3Harris $24M gateway manpacks; Army established NGC2 common data layer baseline on Palantir Foundry (cloud) and Anduril Lattice (tactical) (Jun 2026); at Project Convergence Capstone (Sept 2026) one soldier told Business Insider that connection issues 'either problems with the NGC2 system or the result of electronic warfare and jamming, had left it mostly unusable.' Contract figures are awards/orders, not revenue or proof of scaled deployment.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: For nearly 20 years, the Army has had limited success in developing an information network with sensors, software, and radios to give soldiers needed information.
findings.source_title: GAO-13-179 Army Networks: Size and Scope of Modernization Investment Merit Increased Oversight; Business Insider (Sep 5, 2026) on NGC2 at Project Convergence
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: NGC2 is structured as an ecosystem with named data-layer (Palantir/Anduril) and transport-layer (Persistent, L3Harris) incumbents; entry for a two-person team is via the application layer on top of the common data layer, or via EW-resilience/DDIL tooling that the field reports show is still weak.

findings.title: DoD CIO 'State of DevSecOps' (March 2025): authorizing officials are 'biased to caution,' reciprocity is lacking or unclear, software factories face funding-model limits, and cloud utilization data is hard to obtain
findings.detail: The DoD CIO study (Distribution A) states barriers to continuous ATO include that 'too often, cybersecurity teams, IT infrastructure teams, development teams, leadership, AOs, and DoD Component CISOs don't engage in a collaborative manner'; 'it is a common refrain that AOs are biased to caution rather than biased to action resulting in delays of software capabilities'; on reciprocity, 'common discussion points included lack of reciprocity and cases in which reciprocity guidance was unclear.' It also reports 'software factories face challenges with consistent funding and business models that limit large scale expansion' and that the variety of cloud purchasing mechanisms 'presents a challenge to obtaining utilization data.' The study cites GAO-24-106831 for 75-80% of 40 MDAPs adopting modern practices. A NAVSEA example delivered 13 updates in 9 months to a production cloud.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: It is a common refrain that AOs are 'biased to caution' rather than 'biased to action' resulting in delays of software capabilities.
findings.source_title: DoD CIO, The State of DevSecOps within the Department of Defense (March 2025)
chain_steps: cATO evaluation criteria and implementation guide
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: ATO friction is the most-cited go-to-market blocker for defense software startups; compliance-automation (evidence collection, control inheritance, cATO dashboards) is a real niche, and Onebrief's NGC2 ATO (Jun 2026) shows the path exists but is effortful.

findings.title: DoD AI Strategy memo (Jan 2026): directs a 'wartime approach' to eliminate blockers to data sharing, ATOs, test and certification; federated data catalogs due within 30 days; models deployed within 30 days of release
findings.detail: The Secretary's AI strategy memorandum (published Jan 13, 2026 per Bigdata timestamp) directs: 'We must eliminate blockers to data sharing, Authorizations to Operate (ATOs), test and evaluation and certification, contracting, hiring and talent management'; CDAO to act as 'Wartime CDAO' with the CIO to leverage 'cross-domain data access and rapid ATO reciprocity'; Components to deliver federated data catalogs 'exposing their system interfaces, data assets, and access mechanisms across all classification levels' within 30 days, enforcing the 'DoD Data Decrees' and the May 2021 'Creating Data Advantage' memo; a vendor cadence enabling frontier models 'within 30 days of public release' as a primary procurement criterion; 'any lawful use' contract language within 180 days; deployment velocity metrics reported monthly.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: We must eliminate blockers to data sharing, Authorizations to Operate (ATOs), test and evaluation and certification, contracting, hiring and talent management, and other policies that inhibit rapid experimentation and fielding.
findings.source_title: Department of War, Artificial Intelligence Strategy memorandum (Jan 2026)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Top-down policy now names the exact frictions GAO/IG documented (ATO, data sharing, classification); this raises demand for data-catalog, model-integration and ATO-acceleration products but also favors frontier-model vendors and large integrators with existing accreditations.

findings.title: CRS JADC2 products: IF11493 (In Focus, John R. Hoehn; updated through at least Jan 2025) and R46725 (Background and Issues for Congress) frame service programs (ABMS, Project Convergence, Project Overmatch) and questions on cost, interoperability and requirements
findings.detail: CRS In Focus IF11493 'Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2)' and CRS Report R46725 'Joint All-Domain Command and Control: Background and Issues for Congress' (both by John R. Hoehn) describe JADC2 as DOD's concept to connect sensors from all services into a single network and discuss ABMS, Project Convergence and Project Overmatch. Version 13 of IF11493 exists on congress.gov; a third-party citation gives an update date of January 21, 2025 (MEDIUM confidence). The documents could not be opened from this environment (congress.gov, everycrsreport.com and sgp.fas.org blocked), so the specific 'issues for Congress' text is not quoted. No CRS report dedicated to the Army tactical network/ITN was located; a January 2026 CRS report on tanker tactical data links was cited by Defense One (see F38).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: JADC2 is DOD's concept to connect sensors from all of the military services - Air Force, Army, Marine Corps, Navy, and Space Force - into a single network.
findings.source_title: CRS IF11493 and CRS R46725 (John R. Hoehn)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Congressional framing document set; useful for founders' policy literacy but adds no new technical pain evidence beyond GAO.

findings.title: CRS (Jan 2026): tanker aircraft lack tactical data-link access; connectivity would improve survivability and could serve as a backup information conduit in degraded communications
findings.detail: Defense One (Mar 23, 2026), after a KC-135 crash in Iraq, quoted a January 2026 CRS report: 'the tankers' ability to access tactical data links could increase mission success in contested environments by improving survivability, agility, and situational awareness for command-and-control elements and aircrews ... tanker aircraft could serve as a backup information conduit for other aircraft in a degraded communications environment.' Air Mobility leaders had requested upgraded communications before the crash.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Tanker aircraft could serve as a backup information conduit for other aircraft in a degraded communications environment.
findings.source_title: Defense One, 'KC-135 crash in Iraq spurs calls for communications upgrades' (citing January 2026 CRS report)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Retrofit connectivity for large legacy fleets (tankers, airlifters) is an identifiable, congressionally visible gap; the products are radios/gateways (hardware-heavy, ITAR) more than pure software.

findings.title: Oversight gaps: no 2019-2026 GAO/DoD IG report specific to DCGS, Project Overmatch, NGC2, JWCC performance, contested logistics C2, or Mission Partner Environment findings could be retrieved
findings.detail: DCGS: GAO's public record found in this sweep consists of bid-protest decisions (Palantir USG, B-412746, 2016, describing DCGS-A2; General Dynamics Mission Systems, B-416181, 2018) and GAO-15-282 (2015); GAO-10-500T (2010) noted the Army would not have a fully functional DCGS until 2016. Project Overmatch: GAO's March 2025 Navy unmanned-systems report was classified per Maritime Executive/IndexBox (Jun 2026); the DoD CIO DevSecOps study lists Project Overmatch among DevSecOps-enabled capabilities; no GAO/IG Overmatch findings found. NGC2: no GAO/IG report found (program began 2024-2025). GCCS-J: DODIG-2020-068 'Audit of Security Controls Over the DoD's GCCS-J IT System' exists (2020) but findings were not retrievable. GAO-25-108043 (2025) 'Space Operations: DOD Is Pursuing Efforts to Collaborate with Allies' was located by title only. Public evidence insufficient for all of these; absence of reports is not evidence of absence of problems.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Public evidence insufficient.
findings.source_title: GAO bid protest B-412746 (Palantir USG, Inc.); DODIG-2020-068; GAO-25-108043 (titles only)
chain_steps: Downstream agents with gao.gov/dodig.mil access should fill
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Flags where this evidence file is thin so the study does not over-weight the well-documented programs (JADC2, ABMS, Space C2) relative to programs that are simply less audited.

findings.title: GAO-26-107085 (Jan 2026): Space Development Agency missile-warning constellation risks late delivery; readiness of critical parts overestimated
findings.detail: GAO found DOD 'is developing a new system - a large constellation of satellites - to detect and track missile threats. But its current efforts risk not delivering needed capabilities as quickly as planned. DOD is overestimating the readiness of some parts critical to this system, such as the spacecraft,' causing unplanned work; DOD relies on contractors' schedules to track progress. Relevant to space-based sensing feeding C2/Golden Dome.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DOD is overestimating the readiness of some parts critical to this system, such as the spacecraft. This has resulted in unplanned work - adding time to contractors' schedules.
findings.source_title: Missile Warning Satellites: Space Development Agency Should Be More Realistic and Transparent About Risks to Capability Delivery (GAO-26-107085)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Space-sensor data volume for C2 is arriving later than planned; ground-segment fusion/processing vendors depend on these schedules.

structured.segment_mapping_assumption: The orchestrator's S01-S14 taxonomy was not provided to this agent. IDs are assigned under this working mapping and should be remapped if the study's taxonomy differs: S01 joint/service C2 and battle-management software (JADC2/ABMS/NGC2/COP); S02 tactical transport and networks (ITN, MANET, SATCOM, DDIL, radios, data links); S03 data fabric/data mesh, integration, standards, classification-aware sharing; S04 ISR processing/PED, sensor fusion, track management, friendly-force tracking; S05 space C2 and space-based sensing (SPADOC/ATLAS, SDA); S06 coalition/Mission Partner Environment/cross-domain; S07 PNT; S08 EMSO/EW; S09 cybersecurity, zero trust, ATO/RMF; S10 cloud/edge compute (JWCC); S11 AI/ML decision support and CDAO enterprise AI; S12 logistics/sustainment C2 and enterprise data (Advana/WDP); S13 software acquisition, DevSecOps, MOSA, program oversight; S14 experimentation, test and lessons-learned.
structured.access_constraints_methodology: The research environment's egress proxy blocked gao.gov, files.gao.gov, dodig.mil, media.defense.gov, congress.gov, everycrsreport.com, sgp.fas.org, web.archive.org and all defense news sites; the shared WebSearch budget was exhausted after 12 successful queries and Bigdata.com credits after ~12 useful queries. Report-level facts were therefore triangulated from (a) WebSearch result snippets of gao.gov/dodig.mil pages, (b) the GovHawkDC/gaoreports GitHub mirror of GAO product metadata (title, dates, summary, topics; coverage 2001-early 2026 with gaps), (c) Bigdata.com-indexed copies of GAO product pages and trade-press coverage, (d) a GitHub mirror of the full GAO-21-320SP PDF text, and (e) the DoD CIO State of DevSecOps 2025 text mirrored on GitHub. Where only a title was retrievable the finding says so.
